solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Peak adding singular note to hat

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tone is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a musical note onto the peak of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the singular note is added to the hat, so the hat comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is the top stone of a structure, hence the crowning point or culmination.

clue.text: Point about unique selling point

explanation.surface: A marketer makes a point about a product's unique selling point.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end where two curves meet, so it is a point.

clue.text: Plot after papa gets fresh Covid variant sans name in lab exposure?

indicators.note: sans means without, so the letter abbreviating name is dropped from the variant's label
after places the word for plot at the end, behind everything else

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO alphabet
hot as in fresh, hot off the press

explanation.surface: A scheme in which a new Covid strain is identified in a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: OMICRON loses its final N. The question mark admits that 'exposure' means a photograph rather than infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph taken through a microscope is a laboratory picture, a photographic exposure made in a lab.

clue.text: Mathematician coming round to teaching

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the mathematician's name goes about the short word

explanation.surface: A mathematician is slowly warming to the idea of teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming round to' reads as being persuaded; it is an instruction to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutoring is individual instruction, a form of teaching.

clue.text: Church follows New Testament about Old Nick

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the church abbreviation goes at the end
about means surrounding, so the testament abbreviation goes around the letter for old

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The church follows scripture concerning the Devil.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a name for the Devil, but 'Old' gives a letter and 'Nick' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut, and so is a notch.

clue.text: Client is against a girl returning

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word for girl is read right to left

explanation.surface: A client takes the side against a girl who keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal dependant, and client in its old sense means a dependant under a patron's protection.

clue.text: Tsar shot certainly in error

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of the ruler's title are scattered

parts.note: ay, or aye, means yes, certainly

explanation.surface: The Tsar was shot, certainly by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray is going wrong, so the adverb matches being in error.

clue.text: Iberia's fare is covered by plane width, place of origin and hirer out mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter of the hirer's title goes

parts.note: a plane's width is its wingspan
home is where you come from

explanation.surface: An airline's in-flight meal is paid for by plane width and hiring charges.
explanation.walkthrough: Iberia is also Spain's airline, which makes 'fare' look like a ticket price. In a down clue, 'covered by' means placed below, so the word for plane width sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato omelette called a tortilla is classic food from the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Fruit began going off in truck

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for truck
going off means spoiling or going bad, so the letters of began are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fruit started going rotten inside the delivery truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' fits the surface as fruit spoiling, which hides its job as the rearrangement signal; lorry is the British word for truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A loganberry is a hybrid of blackberry and raspberry, a soft fruit.

clue.text: Front runners in shock photo finish paying out

indicators.note: front runners are the leaders, so the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A shock photo finish on the racecourse sees the bookies paying out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending money is laying it out, the same as paying out.

clue.text: Baseball fielder and items he wears when running?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the infielder placed between second and third base
second meaning, split in two: running kit is a pair of shorts and a top

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, where the word breaks as SHORTS plus TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the fielder stationed between second and third base is called by this name; read in two parts it is jogging clothing.

clue.text: Sharpness about tungsten guitar string's sound

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for sharpness wraps around the element symbol

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten (wolfram)

explanation.surface: A tungsten guitar string gives a sharp, bright sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the resonant vibrating sound of a plucked string.

clue.text: Almost convinced about old tart

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the shortened word surrounds the letter for old
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for convinced is dropped

parts.note: to be sure is to be convinced
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone is all but certain about an old woman of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a noun for a woman in the surface; it is the adjective for a sharp taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart as an adjective means sharp-tasting or acidic, a plain synonym of sour.

clue.text: Put up with song ultimately written like Bartók

parts.note: a picture put up on a wall is hung
an aria is a song in opera

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of written is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tolerant listener endures a song composed in Bartók's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like a single phrase meaning tolerate; 'with' is only the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a composer from Budapest, so his nationality fits the adjective.

clue.text: Our father's around when work's finished

indicators.note: around suggests letters scattered every which way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad is home only once the working day is over.
explanation.definitionFit: After hours means after normal working time has ended.

clue.text: Run-up to the weekend finishes in intimacy

parts.note: Friday, abbreviated, is the day leading up to the weekend

explanation.surface: As the weekend approaches, a closeness reaches its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link but supplies letters, meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Close friendship is a relationship of closeness and familiarity, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Dog bound to be supported by queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top, so the queen's letters go underneath

explanation.surface: A dog is sure to have the Queen's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as certain to be; bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer spaniel is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Card box for footwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the box from which a casino dealer deals cards
second meaning: an item worn on the foot

explanation.surface: A cardboard box for storing a new pair of boots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cardboard shoebox; the card box is the dealer's device at a blackjack table.
explanation.definitionFit: In casinos the dealing box holding several decks is called by the same name as the everyday item worn on the foot.

clue.text: Carved figure from galley regularly about years after long-dead ship

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the kept letters go around the rest
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
after places the years letter behind the ship's name

parts.note: the Argo, Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: An ornamental figure salvaged from a galley that sank years after an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Long-dead ship points to Greek myth: Jason sailed in search of the Golden Fleece aboard it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a grotesque carved stone figure, often a waterspout on a church.

clue.text: See you master lingo finally ready for Italy?

indicators.note: finally points to the end of each word, so the closing letters are the ones kept

parts.note: the last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A farewell before mastering the language to be prepared for a trip to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready means cash, as in ready money, so ready for Italy is Italian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's currency is the single European one, and 'ready' is slang for cash in hand.

clue.text: Concertgoer taking in good artist, one who shapes concert

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the concertgoer word holds the other letters

parts.note: a prommer attends the Proms, the BBC's London summer concert season
G is a standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A concertgoer brings along a good artist, someone who plans the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever chooses the pieces and their order for a concert draws up the programme, so is its programmer.

clue.text: What can grip bridge supports both sides of line

indicators.note: being on both sides of something means flanking it, so the outer word surrounds the letter

explanation.surface: Supports on either side of a line holding up a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are pincers used for gripping, so they are things that can grip.

clue.text: Anticyclone arrives in Scots region

parts.note: an anticyclone is an area of high pressure, a high
a flight arrives when it lands

explanation.surface: A spell of high pressure reaches part of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountainous north and west of Scotland is the region known by this name.

clue.text: Broadcast now so faint

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A transmission comes through now, but very weakly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' reads as a link before the definition, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, especially from emotion.

clue.text: Something valuable chap extracted from beet

indicators.note: extracted from means pulled out of, so one word is taken away from the other

parts.note: a mangold is a kind of beet grown for cattle feed

explanation.surface: A man digs a prize out of a beetroot.
explanation.walkthrough: Mangold (also mangel-wurzel) is a large fodder beet; remove MAN from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is a precious metal and stands for anything of great value.

clue.text: Leave out Bard's title role when mounted in reduced form?

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going up, so the letters run from bottom to top
reduced form means shortened, so the role's last letter is lost

parts.note: Timon of Athens, title character of a Shakespeare play

explanation.surface: Cutting Shakespeare's title role when a shortened version is staged.
explanation.walkthrough: Mounted sounds theatrical, as in staging a production; here it reverses a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out.

clue.text: Prudent to pursue universal employment

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the word for prudent comes after the other letter

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A careful person chases jobs open to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment in the sense of use: the way something is employed is its usage.

clue.text: Drug check protecting friendly community and its environment

indicators.note: protecting means guarding all round, so the outer letters enclose the word for friendly

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: A drug check is protecting a close-knit neighbourhood and its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug and the check join first to make the outer casing; in clues E is the usual shorthand for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the term covers a set of living organisms together with the physical surroundings they interact with.

clue.text: Namely this, metamorphic?

indicators.note: metamorphic means changed in form, so the letters of this are rearranged

parts.note: SC, scilicet, is Latin for namely
the letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: Pointing at a specimen: namely this one, it is metamorphic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the answer is a rock, and the clue points at it as a metamorphic example.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a layered crystalline rock formed by metamorphism, a textbook example of metamorphic rock.

clue.text: Claim during trial about English Republican

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the phrase for during trial surrounds the two letters

parts.note: during the trial is in it
E is the abbreviation for English
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A claim is lodged during a trial about an English Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During trial' is read as a single phrase, in test, and the two abbreviations go inside that whole string rather than inside the trial word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a legal stake or right in something, which is a claim on it.
